'Pay *attention* to the pattern on the door,' she called up to us. We had walked past it twice without noticing — carved into the stone was a map we had been searching for all day.

certain:1.en: Silverfang met us on the open ledge outside the lighthouse, her silver coat bright under the stars. She pointed to a *certain* cluster of lights far below the clouds. 'That group of lamps never moves,' she said. 'It marks a fixed island — a real one, not a drifting ghost.' Old Helm immediately unrolled his chart.

care:1.en: Bell wrapped the newly found word-fragment in soft cloth with great *care*, as if it were made of light itself. The fragment pulsed faintly, warming her hands. Around us the island hummed, and even the wind seemed to slow down to watch.

state:1.en: The old lighthouse stood in a sorry *state*: its lamp was dark, its steps were cracked, and moss covered every stone. Old Helm walked a slow circle around it, saying nothing. I felt sure the lighthouse had once guided whole fleets of sky-ships home.

state:1.line: 'Look at the *state* of this place,' Old Helm said quietly.

impact:1.en: The word-fragment hit the lighthouse stone with a sharp *impact*, and a ring of blue light spread outward across the whole island floor. We stepped back. Slowly, a new path of floating stones rose from the clouds below, pointing toward a distant island none of us had seen before.

impact:1.line: 'Feel that *impact*?' Bell whispered. 'The whole island heard it.'

reason:1.en: I asked Old Helm why the lighthouse had gone dark. He smiled and said there was always a *reason* — we just had to find it. Bell pointed to a hollow in the wall where the word-stone should have sat. Someone had taken it long before we arrived.

reason:1.line: 'There is a *reason* for every darkness,' Old Helm said gently.

close:1.en: Silverfang's ship appeared from the clouds, flying *close* enough that I could see the silver flag snapping in the wind. Old Helm did not flinch. Bell checked her compass twice. We all knew that wherever the word-stone led, Silverfang would not be far behind.

close:1.line: 'They are too *close*,' Bell said. 'We move now.'

individual:1.en: Each word-fragment carried its own *individual* glow — some gold, some pale blue, and one a deep, steady green. No two felt the same in your hand. Bell kept them in separate pockets, saying that mixing them too early would confuse the map and send us somewhere none of us wanted to go.

individual:1.line: 'Each one is *individual*,' Bell said, 'so keep them apart for now.'

area:1.en: We gathered outside the lighthouse and divided the surrounding *area* into four sections to search for the missing word-stone. Old Helm took the cliffs, Bell the tide-pools, and I took the star-moss fields. The wind carried a soft ringing sound from somewhere just beyond the edge.
area:1.cnHint: 众人将灯塔周围的____划分成四块，分头寻找失踪的词语石。

area:1.line: 'Search your *area* completely before you call out,' said Old Helm.

sentences.cn: 风中传来一阵轻微的铃声，从边缘某处飘来。

enable:1.en: At the edge of Windperch Island, Old Helm unrolled a glowing map fragment on a flat stone. 'This word will *enable* us to cross the cloud bridge,' he said, tracing the faint letters with one finger. The whole troupe leaned in, breath held, watching the bridge slowly rise from the mist below.
enable:1.cnHint: 老舵在悬崖边展开地图碎片，发现一个词能____我们穿越云桥。

simple:1.en: Bell knelt beside a cracked signpost at the island's crossroads, studying the carved letters. The answer to the puzzle, she realised, was *simple* — three small words pointing the way north. She laughed softly, surprised that something so easy had kept the troupe guessing for an entire morning.

several:1.en: Old Helm led us through a winding street of lantern-sellers on Amber Shelf Island. We had passed *several* dark doorways before Bell spotted a faint glow behind one of them, too steady to be a candle, too quiet to be a fire. She raised her hand and the troupe stopped.

struggle:1.en: The old rope ladder down to Lantern Dock swayed in the wind, and I could see every rung was slick with dew. My *struggle* to hold on was real — hands burning, boots slipping — but Old Helm's calm voice from below kept me moving one step at a time until solid ground met my feet.

sentences.en: 'The *amount* of words here could map a hundred new islands,' she whispered.
Old Helm placed one careful hand on my shoulder.
sentences.cn: 老舵小心地把一只手放在我的肩膀上。

sentences.en: 'And every one was found by someone just like you.'
sentences.cn: '而且每一个都是像你一样的人找到的。'

point:1.en: Old Helm spread the collected map pieces on the lighthouse floor. He tapped the very centre where all the lines met. 'This is the *point* we have been moving toward all along,' he said, his voice low and warm. Bell and I leaned in. The shape that formed was not an island. It was a door, drawn in starlight, standing in open sky.

point:1.line: 'Look here — this is the *point* where every path we have walked meets.'

role:1.en: Silverfang arrived just as we were about to leave, her ship sliding alongside the lighthouse rock. She looked at the map, then at me. 'Every troupe needs a word-finder,' she said, almost gently. 'That is your *role* now.' Old Helm said nothing, but the small nod he gave me meant more than any speech. I folded the map and tucked it close.

risk:1.en: The old lighthouse leaned over the edge of the floating island, half its base crumbling into open sky. 'We need that beacon to read our map fragment,' said Old Helm. I looked down at the endless drop below. To reach the lamp room, I would have to *risk* a climb along the cracked outer wall.

success:1.en: Bell had mapped the approach three times before dawn. She marked every cracked tile, every gust of wind that swept the lighthouse platform. success:1.line: 'A *success* like this means the next island will show itself,' said Bell.

group:1.en: Three other travellers were already camped at the base of the lighthouse when we arrived — a cartographer, a wind-reader, and a lantern-keeper. Old Helm studied them with quiet eyes. 'Every strong *group* needs different kinds of knowing,' he said, and walked over to introduce us all before the stars shifted overhead.

group:1.hook: The lantern-keeper smiled and said she had been waiting for us.
group:1.line: 'A *group* this varied can solve puzzles none of us could alone,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Three other travellers were already camped at the base of the lighthouse when we arrived — a cartographer, a wind-reader, and a lantern-keeper.
sentences.cn: 我们到灯塔底部时，已经有三个旅人在那儿扎营了——一个制图师、一个读风人，还有一个灯笼守护者。

course:1.en: The map fragment from the lighthouse showed a winding path through three cloud-banks before reaching the next island. Bell traced it with one finger. 'The *course* is longer than I hoped,' she admitted, 'but it curves past the Wind Garden — and that means we can resupply before the cold stretch ahead.'

course:1.hook: Something was already moving along that course — and moving fast.
course:1.line: 'The *course* bends wide, but trust me — it is the safer road,' said Bell.

relationship:1.en: Silverfang's ship had been circling the lighthouse island since morning. He and Old Helm stood a short distance apart on the stone platform, speaking in low, careful voices. relationship:1.hook: Silverfang glanced back once, and his expression was hard to read.
relationship:1.line: 'Our *relationship* goes back further than this troupe does,' said Old Helm.

form:1.en: The lighthouse door was sealed with a strange lock — a flat stone panel covered in carved symbols. Bell ran her hand across it slowly. 'Each symbol is a letter,' she said, 'and together they *form* a word that must be spoken aloud.' The wind held still, as if the island itself was listening.

form:1.hook: She whispered the word, and the stone door began to breathe.
form:1.line: 'These carvings *form* the oldest word in any map we have carried,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The lighthouse door was sealed with a strange lock — a flat stone panel covered in carved symbols.
sentences.cn: 灯塔的门用一把奇怪的锁封着——一块平的石头面板上刻满了符号。

interest:1.en: Old Helm did not often stop walking, but the carved mural along the lighthouse wall made him pause. He leaned close, reading lines of ancient script that described the first travellers to cross these skies. 'I have a deep *interest* in whoever built this place,' he murmured, almost to himself, as the stars above brightened.
interest:1.cnHint: 灯塔外墙的壁画让老舵长驻足，他说自己对建造这座灯塔的人有着深厚的____。
interest:1.hook: One face in the mural looked unsettlingly familiar.
interest:1.line: 'My *interest* in this lighthouse began long before we arrived here,' said Old Helm.

simply:1.en: The beacon at the top of the lighthouse had not turned in years; its gears were clogged with salt and dust. I expected a long repair, but Bell opened a small panel, pressed two brass buttons, and the whole mechanism hummed to life. Some things, I realised, are *simply* waiting for someone willing to try.

simply:1.hook: The light swept out — and landed on a shape in the clouds.
simply:1.line: 'It was *simply* waiting for steady hands and a little courage,' said Bell.

conversation:2.line: 'That *conversation* was never finished,' Old Helm said softly.

self:2.line: 'Your *self* is the compass that never breaks,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: 'Some steps must be taken,' he said, and crossed it.
sentences.cn: "有些步子是必须走的，"他说，然后走过去了。

sentences.en: To find the word carved on the other side, I had to *risk* the crossing too.

success:2.en: Bell spread the old map across the lighthouse floor and pointed to a sealed brass box in the corner. Inside, folded around a single carved word, was a note: 'Every *success* on these islands begins with one honest question.' Old Helm read it twice, then smiled at the ceiling.
success:2.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔里打开一个铜盒，里面的纸条写着关于____的秘密。
success:2.hook: Old Helm's smile faded as he flipped the note over.
success:2.line: 'Every *success* here begins with one honest question.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the old map across the lighthouse floor and pointed to a sealed brass box in the corner.
sentences.cn: 小铃把那张古老的地图铺在灯塔的地板上，指向角落里一个密封的黄铜盒子。

sentences.en: Inside, folded around a single carved word, was a note: 'Every *success* on these islands begins with one honest question.'
Old Helm read it twice, then smiled at the ceiling.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍，然后对着天花板微笑。

group:2.en: A *group* of small signal lamps hung in a circle inside the lighthouse top, each one a different colour. Bell said the pattern they made was a language. Old Helm studied them quietly, then began matching each colour to a letter on the map fragment. The message slowly came clear.
group:2.cnHint: 灯塔顶部悬挂的一____彩色信号灯，排列成某种隐藏的语言。
group:2.hook: The last lamp flickered and went dark.
group:2.line: 'This *group* of lamps is spelling something out for us.'

sentences.en: A *group* of small signal lamps hung in a circle inside the lighthouse top, each one a different colour.
Bell said the pattern they made was a language.
sentences.cn: 小铃说它们排成的图案是一种语言。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied them quietly, then began matching each colour to a letter on the map fragment.
sentences.cn: 老舵静静地研究了一会儿，然后开始把每种颜色和地图碎片上的字母对应起来。

sentences.en: The message slowly came clear.
sentences.cn: 信息慢慢浮现出来了。

course:2.en: The lighthouse keeper had left a log, its pages soft with salt air. The final entry described a *course* across the sky — a precise route from lamp-flash to lamp-flash — that led to an island no chart showed. Bell traced the line with one careful finger and looked up at us.
course:2.cnHint: 守灯人的航海日志里，记录了一条通往未知岛屿的____。
course:2.hook: Bell's finger stopped at a blank space on the map.
course:2.line: 'Follow the *course* in the log and the hidden island will appear.'

sentences.en: The lighthouse keeper had left a log, its pages soft with salt air.
sentences.cn: 灯塔守塔人留下了一份日志，纸页被盐风吹得柔软。

sentences.en: The final entry described a *course* across the sky — a precise route from lamp-flash to lamp-flash — that led to an island no chart showed.
Bell traced the line with one careful finger and looked up at us.
sentences.cn: 小铃用一根细心的手指描绘着那条线，然后抬起头看着我们。

relationship:2.en: Carved into the lighthouse wall were two symbols we had seen before on different islands. Old Helm stood back and folded his arms. 'There is a *relationship* between these two signs,' he said slowly. 'One is a key. The other is the lock.' Bell immediately began searching for a third symbol.
relationship:2.cnHint: 老舵发现墙上两个符号之间存在____，就像钥匙和锁一样。
relationship:2.hook: Bell found the third symbol behind a loose brick.
relationship:2.line: 'There is a *relationship* between these signs — one opens the other.'

sentences.en: Carved into the lighthouse wall were two symbols we had seen before on different islands.
sentences.cn: 刻在灯塔墙上的两个符号，我们之前在不同的岛屿上见过。

sentences.en: Old Helm stood back and folded his arms.
sentences.cn: 老舵往后站了一步，交叉放好双臂。

sentences.en: 'There is a *relationship* between these two signs,' he said slowly.
'One is a key.
sentences.cn: "其中一个是钥匙。

sentences.en: The other is the lock.'
sentences.cn: 另一个是锁。"

sentences.en: Bell immediately began searching for a third symbol.
sentences.cn: 小铃立刻开始搜寻第三个符号。

form:2.en: Dust on the lighthouse shelf held a perfect outline — the *form* of a small object, long since removed. Around it, tiny scratched arrows pointed toward the window. Whatever had rested there had been important enough for someone to mark its exact shape before taking it away.
form:2.cnHint: 搁架上的灰尘保留着一个已消失物品的____，周围还有指向窗外的刻痕。
form:2.hook: The arrows all pointed to the same dark cloud.
form:2.line: 'Look — the *form* left in the dust tells us exactly what was taken.'

sentences.en: Dust on the lighthouse shelf held a perfect outline — the *form* of a small object, long since removed.
Around it, tiny scratched arrows pointed toward the window.
sentences.cn: 在它周围，细小的刻画箭头指向窗户。

sentences.en: Whatever had rested there had been important enough for someone to mark its exact shape before taking it away.
sentences.cn: 不管什么东西曾经放在那里，都重要到有人在拿走它之前标记下了它的确切形状。

interest:2.en: Old Helm picked up a glass bottle from the lighthouse floor. Inside was a rolled note that simply said: 'If this finds someone with *interest* in the truth, look beneath the fourth step.' He set the bottle down very carefully and turned to us with bright eyes and said nothing at all.
interest:2.cnHint: 老舵发现一个玻璃瓶，里面的字条说只有对真相有____的人才能找到答案。
interest:2.hook: None of us moved toward the fourth step.
interest:2.line: 'If you have *interest* in the truth, look beneath the fourth step.'

sentences.en: Old Helm picked up a glass bottle from the lighthouse floor.
sentences.cn: 老舵从灯塔的地板上捡起一个玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside was a rolled note that simply said: 'If this finds someone with *interest* in the truth, look beneath the fourth step.'
He set the bottle down very carefully and turned to us with bright eyes and said nothing at all.
sentences.cn: 他小心翼翼地放下瓶子，转向我们，眼睛闪闪发亮，什么都没有说。

simply:2.en: Bell had been quiet for an hour, studying the lighthouse lens. Then she laughed softly. 'The message was *simply* here all along,' she said, tilting the lens until light fell on the wall in the shape of an arrow and a word. Old Helm shook his head — not in doubt, but in wonder.
simply:2.cnHint: 小铃倾斜镜片后发现，答案____就藏在光影里，一直等着被看见。
simply:2.hook: The arrow of light pointed straight down.
simply:2.line: 'The message was *simply* here, waiting in the light all along.'

sentences.en: Bell had been quiet for an hour, studying the lighthouse lens.
sentences.cn: 小铃已经安静地看了一个小时的灯塔透镜。

sentences.en: Then she laughed softly.
sentences.cn: 然后她轻声笑了。

sentences.en: 'The message was *simply* here all along,' she said, tilting the lens until light fell on the wall in the shape of an arrow and a word.
Old Helm shook his head — not in doubt, but in wonder.
sentences.cn: 老舵摇了摇头——不是怀疑，而是惊叹。

survey:2.en: Inside the old lighthouse, a rolled map lay on the floor. Old Helm knelt beside it and began to *survey* every line and mark, tracing paths between islands none of us had visited. His eyes moved slowly, missing nothing. When he finally looked up, his face held a quiet kind of certainty.
survey:2.cnHint: 老舵长在灯塔内仔细____一张旧地图，发现了从未到访的航线。
survey:2.hook: One island on the map had no name at all.
survey:2.line: 'We must *survey* every mark before we move a single step,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Inside the old lighthouse, a rolled map lay on the floor.
sentences.cn: 在古老的灯塔内，一张卷起的地图躺在地板上。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt beside it and began to *survey* every line and mark, tracing paths between islands none of us had visited.
His eyes moved slowly, missing nothing.
sentences.cn: 他的眼睛缓缓扫过，没有遗漏任何细节。

sentences.en: When he finally looked up, his face held a quiet kind of certainty.
sentences.cn: 当他终于抬起头时，脸上带着一种安静而笃定的神情。

care:2.en: Bell found a small glass bottle wedged between the lighthouse stones. Inside was a folded note, dry and unbroken. Someone had sealed it with great *care*, as though they knew the message might wait years before the right hands opened it. Bell held it close to the star-light to read.
care:2.cnHint: 领航员在灯石缝中发现一只封存严密的瓶中信，感受到写信人的____。
care:2.hook: The handwriting matched no one any of us had ever met.
care:2.line: 'Whoever left this took real *care* to keep it safe,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell found a small glass bottle wedged between the lighthouse stones.
sentences.cn: 小铃在灯塔石缝中找到了一个小玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside was a folded note, dry and unbroken.
sentences.cn: 里面装着一张折叠的纸条，干燥而完整。

sentences.en: Someone had sealed it with great *care*, as though they knew the message might wait years before the right hands opened it.
Bell held it close to the star-light to read.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它靠近星光来阅读。

state:2.en: The lighthouse beam had been dark for a long time. Old Helm checked every gear inside and shook his head at the *state* of the old machinery — rust covered the joints, and two small cogs had cracked clean through. Still, he said nothing was beyond fixing if we worked together.
state:2.cnHint: 老舵长检查灯塔内部装置，对其____感到忧虑，但仍然充满信心。
state:2.hook: A low hum began before anyone touched a single gear.
state:2.line: 'Look at the *state* of these gears — but I have seen worse,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The lighthouse beam had been dark for a long time.
sentences.cn: 灯塔的光束已经熄灭很久了。

sentences.en: Old Helm checked every gear inside and shook his head at the *state* of the old machinery — rust covered the joints, and two small cogs had cracked clean through.
Still, he said nothing was beyond fixing if we worked together.
sentences.cn: 不过他说只要我们一起动手，什么都修得好。

impact:2.en: Bell pressed the old lens back into its frame, and with a soft click it locked. The moment the beam returned, its *impact* on the clouds above was immediate — colours spread outward, and far across the sky, two other island lights blinked on as if in answer. Nobody had expected that.
impact:2.cnHint: 领航员修好灯塔透镜，光束重现所产生的____令整片星空都随之改变。
impact:2.hook: Something enormous shifted behind the furthest cloud.
impact:2.line: 'I never expected the *impact* to reach that far,' said Bell softly.

sentences.en: Bell pressed the old lens back into its frame, and with a soft click it locked.
sentences.cn: 小铃把老透镜装回了镜框，伴随一声轻微的咔哒声锁上了。

sentences.en: The moment the beam returned, its *impact* on the clouds above was immediate — colours spread outward, and far across the sky, two other island lights blinked on as if in answer.
Nobody had expected that.
sentences.cn: 没人预料到会这样。

reason:2.en: Old Helm stared at the message we had found. It was written in plain words, yet one line made no sense: 'Do not light the lamp.' He read it three times, then set it down. 'There is a *reason* behind this warning,' he said. 'We just do not know it yet.'
reason:2.cnHint: 老舵长在瓶中信里发现一句奇怪的警告，努力寻找其中的____。
reason:2.hook: Outside, the lamp had already been lit.
reason:2.line: 'There must be a *reason* someone went to all this trouble,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Old Helm stared at the message we had found.
sentences.cn: 老舵盯着我们找到的信息看。

sentences.en: It was written in plain words, yet one line made no sense: 'Do not light the lamp.'
sentences.cn: 字很清楚，但有一行让人费解："不要点亮灯"。

sentences.en: He read it three times, then set it down.
sentences.cn: 他读了三遍，然后放下了。

sentences.en: 'There is a *reason* behind this warning,' he said.
'We just do not know it yet.'
sentences.cn: "我们只是还不知道原因罢了。"

close:2.en: The lighthouse sat at the very edge of the island, and the drop below was steep. Bell guided us along the narrow path with steady hands, keeping the group *close* together. The wind pushed hard from the left, but nobody slipped. When we reached the door, we all breathed out at once.
close:2.cnHint: 领航员带领大家沿险路前行，让所有人保持____以确保安全。
close:2.hook: The door opened before Bell even reached for the handle.
close:2.line: 'Stay *close* — the edge is nearer than it looks,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The lighthouse sat at the very edge of the island, and the drop below was steep.
sentences.cn: 灯塔坐落在岛屿的最边缘，下面的悬崖陡峭。

sentences.en: Bell guided us along the narrow path with steady hands, keeping the group *close* together.
The wind pushed hard from the left, but nobody slipped.
sentences.cn: 风从左边猛烈吹来，但没人滑倒。

sentences.en: When we reached the door, we all breathed out at once.
sentences.cn: 当我们到达门口时，大家一起松了口气。

individual:2.en: Inside the lighthouse, the walls were covered in small drawings — one for each island in the chain. Old Helm studied them quietly and then said that each *individual* drawing must have been made on location, by someone who had actually stood on every island. That meant someone had been everywhere we hoped to go.
individual:2.cnHint: 灯塔墙上布满小图，老舵长认为每一幅____图画都来自亲身到访的人。
individual:2.hook: One drawing showed an island none of our maps included.
individual:2.line: 'Each *individual* drawing tells its own story,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Inside the lighthouse, the walls were covered in small drawings — one for each island in the chain.
sentences.cn: 灯塔的墙壁上布满了小图画——一个岛屿一幅。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied them quietly and then said that each *individual* drawing must have been made on location, by someone who had actually stood on every island.
That meant someone had been everywhere we hoped to go.
sentences.cn: 这意味着有人去过我们希望去的每一个地方。

area:2.en: Bell unfolded the lighthouse keeper's last chart. A wide *area* in the centre of the sky-sea had been circled and marked with a single word: 'wait.' Nothing else was written there. No islands, no routes, no depths. Just empty space, circled with such care that the ink had gone right through the paper.
area:2.cnHint: 领航员发现航海图上一片被圈出的____，上面只写着一个字——等。
area:2.hook: Silverfang's ship had last been seen heading straight for that circle.
area:2.line: 'That *area* has been circled more than once,' said Bell slowly.

sentences.en: Bell unfolded the lighthouse keeper's last chart.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开了灯塔守护者最后的海图。

sentences.en: A wide *area* in the centre of the sky-sea had been circled and marked with a single word: 'wait.'
Nothing else was written there.
sentences.cn: 别的什么都没写。

sentences.en: No islands, no routes, no depths.
sentences.cn: 没有岛屿，没有航线，没有水深。

sentences.en: Just empty space, circled with such care that the ink had gone right through the paper.
sentences.cn: 只有空白的空间，被如此用心地画了圆，墨水都穿透了纸张。

popular:2.en: The old lighthouse keeper had left behind a message board covered in notes from travellers. One route — threading through the Crystal Arch islands — was marked so many times it had worn through the paper. 'This must be the most *popular* path in the whole sky,' I said, counting the marks with wide eyes. Bell smiled and began to chart our course.
popular:2.cnHint: 我们在灯塔里发现了一块留言板，上面某条航线的标记多得把纸都磨破了，贝尔决定沿着这条____的路线出发。
popular:2.hook: But one note, written in red, warned us to turn back.
popular:2.line: 'This is the most *popular* route — every troupe has tried it.'

sentences.en: The old lighthouse keeper had left behind a message board covered in notes from travellers.
sentences.cn: 老灯塔守护者留下了一块覆满旅客笔记的留言板。

sentences.en: One route — threading through the Crystal Arch islands — was marked so many times it had worn through the paper.
sentences.cn: 一条穿过水晶拱岛屿的航线被标记了无数次，几乎磨穿了纸张。

sentences.en: 'This must be the most *popular* path in the whole sky,' I said, counting the marks with wide eyes.
Bell smiled and began to chart our course.
sentences.cn: 小铃笑了，开始规划我们的路线。

current:2.en: Inside the lighthouse base, a bronze disc lay on the floor, etched with a spiral. Old Helm knelt and traced its grooves. 'The *current* state of the sky lanes changes every season,' he said quietly, 'but this disc updates itself — watch.' The grooves shifted, and a new island blinked into the centre of the map.
current:2.cnHint: 老舵手在灯塔底部找到一块会自动更新的铜盘，显示出____状态的天空航道，以及一座新岛屿的位置。
current:2.hook: The island it revealed had no name — only a blinking amber light.
current:2.line: 'The *current* map is already changing — we must move now.'

sentences.cn: 老舵跪下来描摹它的沟槽。

sentences.cn: 沟槽移动了，一个新的岛屿在地图的中心闪现。

difficult:2.en: A locked iron box sat at the top of the lighthouse stairs, wrapped in a chain of knotted rope. Every knot was a different kind. Bell pulled at the first loop, then laughed softly. 'It is *difficult* to open, but not impossible — each knot is also a letter.' We untied them in order and spelled out the name of a hidden island.
difficult:2.cnHint: 贝尔在灯塔顶部发现一个铁箱，每个绳结都是一个字母，解开这个____的谜题后，拼出了一座隐藏岛屿的名字。
difficult:2.hook: The final knot refused to move, as if the box did not want to be found.
difficult:2.line: 'It looks *difficult*, but every knot here is a clue.'

sentences.en: A locked iron box sat at the top of the lighthouse stairs, wrapped in a chain of knotted rope.
sentences.cn: 一个上了锁的铁盒子放在灯塔楼梯顶端，用打了结的绳子缠绕着。

We untied them in order and spelled out the name of a hidden island.
sentences.cn: 我们按顺序解开了这些结，拼出了一个隐秘岛屿的名字。

amount:2.en: Scattered across the lighthouse floor were hundreds of tiny glass beads, each one engraved with a number. Silverfang gathered them into a jar and held it to the starlight. 'The *amount* of beads matches the distance to the next island — one bead for every sky-mile,' she said. I counted with her, and the number took my breath away.
amount:2.cnHint: 竞争船长把灯塔地板上散落的玻璃珠收进罐子，发现珠子的____恰好等于到下一座岛屿的距离。
amount:2.hook: The number was far greater than any distance we had ever sailed.
amount:2.line: 'The *amount* of beads tells us exactly how far we must go.'

sentences.en: Scattered across the lighthouse floor were hundreds of tiny glass beads, each one engraved with a number.
sentences.cn: 灯塔地板上散落着数百颗玻璃珠，每一颗上都刻着一个数字。

sentences.cn: 银牙把它们集中到一个罐子里，举到星光下。

sentences.en: 'The *amount* of beads matches the distance to the next island — one bead for every sky-mile,' she said.
I counted with her, and the number took my breath away.
sentences.cn: 我和她一起数着，那个数字让我屏住了呼吸。

point:2.en: Pinned to the lighthouse wall was a hand-drawn chart with a single red dot near its edge. Old Helm tapped it once. 'That *point* on the map — that tiny mark — is where the keeper saw a new island rise from the clouds last winter,' he said. I leaned close. The dot pulsed faintly, as though it were still breathing.
point:2.cnHint: 老舵手指着航图边缘一个红色的____说，那里曾有人亲眼看见一座新岛从云中升起。
point:2.hook: As we watched, the red dot moved — slowly, but unmistakably — toward us.
point:2.line: 'Every *point* on this chart was earned by someone brave enough to look.'

sentences.en: 'That *point* on the map — that tiny mark — is where the keeper saw a new island rise from the clouds last winter,' he said.

sentences.en: The dot pulsed faintly, as though it were still breathing.
sentences.cn: 那个红点微微发光，仿佛还在呼吸。

role:2.en: Inside a dusty drawer I found a logbook listing every keeper who had tended this lighthouse. Each name had a note beside it: navigator, caller, signal-watcher. role:2.hook: Beneath my name, the pen moved on its own and wrote one single word.
role:2.line: 'Your *role* in this troupe is only just beginning — keep that page open.'

sentences.en: Inside a dusty drawer I found a logbook listing every keeper who had tended this lighthouse.
sentences.cn: 在一个布满灰尘的抽屉里，我发现了一本日志，记录了照看这座灯塔的每一任守塔人。

sentences.en: Each name had a note beside it: navigator, caller, signal-watcher.
sentences.cn: 每个名字旁边都有注记：航海家、报信员、信号观察员。

enable:2.en: At the base of the old lighthouse, Bell found a copper key tied to a bundle of star charts. 'These charts *enable* us to read the light signals,' she said, spreading them across the stone floor. The patterns matched the flashes above — a message left by someone long before us.
enable:2.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔底部发现了铜钥匙和星图，它们____我们解读灯光信号。
enable:2.hook: But the last signal pointed somewhere no chart had ever shown.
enable:2.line: 'These charts *enable* us to read every flash the lighthouse sends.'

sentences.en: At the base of the old lighthouse, Bell found a copper key tied to a bundle of star charts.
sentences.cn: 在古老灯塔的底部，小铃找到了一把铜钥匙，绑在一捆星图上。

sentences.en: 'These charts *enable* us to read the light signals,' she said, spreading them across the stone floor.
The patterns matched the flashes above — a message left by someone long before us.
sentences.cn: 图案与上方的闪光相匹配——这是很久以前某个人留下的讯息。

simple:2.en: Old Helm lifted a wooden box from behind the lighthouse door. Inside was a *simple* brass dial with four notches and a single arrow. No lock, no trap — just that quiet dial waiting to be turned. Sometimes the strangest discoveries hide inside the plainest things.
simple:2.cnHint: 老舵在灯塔门后发现了一个____的黄铜表盘，等待着被转动。
simple:2.hook: When the arrow clicked to the fourth notch, the floor began to hum.
simple:2.line: 'It looks *simple*, but every notch must be turned in the right order.'

sentences.en: Old Helm lifted a wooden box from behind the lighthouse door.
sentences.cn: 老舵从灯塔门后抬起一个木箱。

sentences.en: Inside was a *simple* brass dial with four notches and a single arrow.
No lock, no trap — just that quiet dial waiting to be turned.
sentences.cn: 没有锁，没有陷阱——只有那个安静的表盘等着被转动。

sentences.en: Sometimes the strangest discoveries hide inside the plainest things.
sentences.cn: 有时候，最奇异的发现就藏在最平凡的东西里面。

several:2.en: Bell counted the lighthouse windows from the ground: *several* panes were dark, but one burned with a pale blue light no candle could make. She marked each dark window on her map. The blue one sat exactly in the middle — as if it had been left on just for us.
several:2.cnHint: 小铃数了数灯塔的窗户，发现____扇是暗的，唯独中间那扇透着蓝光。
several:2.hook: The blue light blinked once, then went dark before anyone could reach it.
several:2.line: 'I have checked *several* windows — only the middle one still burns blue.'

sentences.en: Bell counted the lighthouse windows from the ground: *several* panes were dark, but one burned with a pale blue light no candle could make.
She marked each dark window on her map.
sentences.cn: 她在地图上标记了每个漆黑的窗口。

sentences.en: The blue one sat exactly in the middle — as if it had been left on just for us.
sentences.cn: 那个蓝色的窗口恰好在中间——好像是特地为我们点亮的。

struggle:2.en: The iron door of the lighthouse had not been opened in years. Old Helm and I pushed together, and I felt the real *struggle* — not just the weight of the door, but the feeling that something on the other side did not want to be found. Then, with a groan, it gave way.
struggle:2.cnHint: 灯塔铁门多年未开，我们齐力推门，感受到了一场真正的____。
struggle:2.hook: A folded letter, still sealed, lay just inside on the dusty floor.
struggle:2.line: 'Every great find begins with a *struggle* — push harder and do not stop.'

sentences.en: The iron door of the lighthouse had not been opened in years.
sentences.cn: 灯塔的铁门已经很多年没有打开过了。

sentences.en: Old Helm and I pushed together, and I felt the real *struggle* — not just the weight of the door, but the feeling that something on the other side did not want to be found.
Then, with a groan, it gave way.
sentences.cn: 然后，伴随着一声呻吟，它让开了。

decision:2.en: At the top of the lighthouse stood two levers: one would send a signal west toward the star harbour, the other east toward open sky. Bell looked at Old Helm. He looked at me. The *decision* fell to no one in particular — and somehow that made it heavier than ever.
decision:2.cnHint: 灯塔顶端有两根操纵杆，这个____落在了我们每个人身上。
decision:2.hook: I reached out, closed my eyes, and pulled the lever on the left.
decision:2.line: 'This *decision* is ours to make — choose the signal and do not look back.'

sentences.en: At the top of the lighthouse stood two levers: one would send a signal west toward the star harbour, the other east toward open sky.
sentences.cn: 灯塔顶部站着两根杆子：一根会向西朝星港发信号，另一根向东朝开阔的天空。

sentences.en: Bell looked at Old Helm.
sentences.cn: 小铃看向老舵。

sentences.en: He looked at me.
sentences.cn: 他看向我。

sentences.en: The *decision* fell to no one in particular — and somehow that made it heavier than ever.

kid:2.en: Tucked behind a cracked lighthouse brick we found a small journal. The handwriting was unsteady, like a *kid* just learning to write, yet every entry described the islands with sharp, careful detail. Someone very young had once kept watch here — and had left these words for whoever came next.
kid:2.cnHint: 灯塔砖缝里藏着一本日记，字迹像____写的，却详细记录着群岛的秘密。
kid:2.hook: The final entry read: 'If you found this, the light is yours to carry.'
kid:2.line: 'Only a brave *kid* could have climbed this high and written all of this.'

sentences.en: Tucked behind a cracked lighthouse brick we found a small journal.
sentences.cn: 我们在裂开的灯塔砖后面找到了一本小日记。

sentences.en: The handwriting was unsteady, like a *kid* just learning to write, yet every entry described the islands with sharp, careful detail.
Someone very young had once kept watch here — and had left these words for whoever came next.
sentences.cn: 曾经有个很小的孩子在这里守过灯——他留下了这些字，给后来的人。

ability:2.en: The lighthouse lens was cracked in three places, yet it still turned. Bell studied it and said the old builder must have had a rare *ability* — to shape glass so that even broken, it bends light the right way. We stood in the spinning colours and felt, just briefly, like we understood something large.
ability:2.cnHint: 灯塔镜片虽已碎裂，小铃说建造者拥有非凡的____，使它依然能折射光芒。
ability:2.hook: Then one shard fell free and the whole lens began to spin faster.
ability:2.line: 'The builder had an *ability* we may never fully understand — but we can honour it.'

sentences.en: The lighthouse lens was cracked in three places, yet it still turned.
sentences.cn: 灯塔的透镜在三个地方有裂纹，但它依然在转动。

sentences.en: Bell studied it and said the old builder must have had a rare *ability* — to shape glass so that even broken, it bends light the right way.
We stood in the spinning colours and felt, just briefly, like we understood something large.
sentences.cn: 我们站在旋转的色彩中，短暂地感到自己理解了什么宏大的东西。

task:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a scroll found beneath the lighthouse lamp. It listed one *task* in plain letters: relight the beacon before the next tide or the passage between the islands would close for a season. We had no lamp oil. We had two hours. We had each other.
task:2.cnHint: 老舵在灯塔灯座下发现了一张卷轴，上面只写着一个____：在下次涨潮前重新点亮灯塔。
task:2.hook: Silverfang's ship appeared on the horizon — and she was moving faster than us.
task:2.line: 'Our *task* is clear: relight this beacon before the tide turns against us.'

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a scroll found beneath the lighthouse lamp.
sentences.cn: 老舵展开了在灯塔灯下找到的一卷纸。

sentences.en: It listed one *task* in plain letters: relight the beacon before the next tide or the passage between the islands would close for a season.
We had no lamp oil.
sentences.cn: 我们没有灯油。

sentences.en: We had two hours.
sentences.cn: 我们只有两小时。

sentences.en: We had each other.
sentences.cn: 我们有彼此。

put:2.en: Bell lifted the old lantern from its hook and *put* it on the stone table at the centre of the lighthouse. The moment it touched the surface, lines of light spread outward like rivers on a map, tracing the shapes of three islands none of us had seen before. Old Helm leaned close and whispered that the lantern had been waiting for exactly this spot.
put:2.cnHint: 小铃将灯笼____在石桌上，光线随即蔓延成一幅新地图。
put:2.hook: The third island's outline flickered, then slowly went dark.
put:2.line: '*Put* it right here — the stone remembers the shape.'

sentences.en: Bell lifted the old lantern from its hook and *put* it on the stone table at the centre of the lighthouse.
The moment it touched the surface, lines of light spread outward like rivers on a map, tracing the shapes of three islands none of us had seen before.
sentences.cn: 它刚一接触到石桌，光线就向四周蔓延开去，就像地图上的河流，勾勒出三个我们都没见过的岛屿的轮廓。

sentences.en: Old Helm leaned close and whispered that the lantern had been waiting for exactly this spot.
sentences.cn: 老舵凑近了，低声说灯笼一直在等这个位置。

difference:2.en: Old Helm held two lighthouse keys side by side. At first glance they looked the same, but Bell pointed out the tiny notch on the second one. 'That *difference* is everything,' she said. We tried the notched key, and the heavy iron door swung open to reveal a room full of floating glass jars, each one holding a glowing word.
difference:2.cnHint: 两把钥匙看似相同，但那点小小的____决定了能否打开门。
difference:2.hook: Inside the last jar, a word pulsed that no one in the troupe recognised.
difference:2.line: 'One small *difference* and the whole door changes — look closely.'

sentences.en: Old Helm held two lighthouse keys side by side.
sentences.cn: 老舵把两把灯塔钥匙并排放在一起。

sentences.en: At first glance they looked the same, but Bell pointed out the tiny notch on the second one.
sentences.cn: 乍一看它们一模一样，但小铃指出第二把钥匙上有个细微的缺口。

sentences.en: 'That *difference* is everything,' she said.
We tried the notched key, and the heavy iron door swung open to reveal a room full of floating glass jars, each one holding a glowing word.
sentences.cn: 我们用了有缺口的那把钥匙，沉重的铁门就打开了，里面是一整间漂浮的玻璃罐子，每个罐子里都装着一个闪闪发光的字。

lack:2.en: The message we found rolled inside the lighthouse torch was short: the island ahead had light, had water, had warmth — but its *lack* of a landing stone meant no ship had ever stayed. Silverfang traced the words with one finger, then grinned. Old Helm was already sketching a rope ladder in the margin of the map.
lack:2.cnHint: 前方小岛什么都有，唯独____停船石，让人犯难。
lack:2.hook: Silverfang folded the message and said the rope ladder idea just might work.
lack:2.line: 'A *lack* of one stone should not stop us — we adapt.'

sentences.en: The message we found rolled inside the lighthouse torch was short: the island ahead had light, had water, had warmth — but its *lack* of a landing stone meant no ship had ever stayed.
Silverfang traced the words with one finger, then grinned.
sentences.cn: 银牙用一根手指描过这些字，然后咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: Old Helm was already sketching a rope ladder in the margin of the map.
sentences.cn: 老舵已经在地图的空白处画起绳梯了。

case:2.en: Tucked behind the lighthouse stairs we found a wooden *case* no bigger than a bread loaf. Inside, wrapped in soft cloth, lay seven small tiles, each carved with a letter. Arranged in order they spelled a word that lit up gold the moment Bell read it aloud, and a new dot appeared on our shared map like a star switching on.
case:2.cnHint: 楼梯后藏着一个小木____，里面的字母拼出了新地图坐标。
case:2.hook: The gold light faded fast — we had maybe one minute to copy the location.
case:2.line: 'Open the *case* carefully — the tiles inside are older than the island.'

sentences.en: Tucked behind the lighthouse stairs we found a wooden *case* no bigger than a bread loaf.
Inside, wrapped in soft cloth, lay seven small tiles, each carved with a letter.
sentences.cn: 里面用软布包裹着七块小瓷砖，每块上面都刻着一个字母。

sentences.en: Arranged in order they spelled a word that lit up gold the moment Bell read it aloud, and a new dot appeared on our shared map like a star switching on.
sentences.cn: 按顺序排列起来拼成一个词，小铃大声读出来的那一刻，这个词就闪闪发光地变成了金色，我们共用的地图上又出现了一个新的点，就像一颗星星亮了起来。

sure:2.en: I stared at the two staircases inside the lighthouse, unsure which led to the signal room. Bell was *sure* the left one was right because the steps were worn smoother — more feet, more years, more use. She was correct. At the top we found the brass signal mirror still aimed at an island none of our maps had named yet.
sure:2.cnHint: 面对两条楼梯，小铃____地选择了左边那条，结果证明她是对的。
sure:2.hook: The mirror's aim pointed past every island we had ever visited.
sure:2.line: 'I am *sure* — worn steps always mean the right way.'

sentences.en: I stared at the two staircases inside the lighthouse, unsure which led to the signal room.
sentences.cn: 我盯着灯塔里的两段楼梯，不确定哪一段通向信号室。

sentences.en: Bell was *sure* the left one was right because the steps were worn smoother — more feet, more years, more use.
She was correct.
sentences.cn: 她是对的。

sentences.en: At the top we found the brass signal mirror still aimed at an island none of our maps had named yet.
sentences.cn: 楼梯顶端，那面黄铜信号镜仍然瞄准着我们地图上还没命名的一个岛屿。

enough:2.en: Old Helm counted our remaining word-tiles by the lighthouse window: seven. He said seven was *enough* to unlock the passage to the eastern reef island, but only if we used them in the right order. Bell arranged them on the sill, and one by one the tiles began to hum, casting small coloured shadows on the wall like a quiet celebration.
enough:2.cnHint: 老舵手数了数字母砖，确认数量____，可以开启东礁岛的通道。
enough:2.hook: The last tile hummed louder than all the others combined.
enough:2.line: 'Seven is *enough* — trust the count and place them now.'

sentences.en: Old Helm counted our remaining word-tiles by the lighthouse window: seven.
sentences.cn: 老舵在灯塔窗边清点我们剩下的字牌：七块。

sentences.en: He said seven was *enough* to unlock the passage to the eastern reef island, but only if we used them in the right order.
Bell arranged them on the sill, and one by one the tiles began to hum, casting small coloured shadows on the wall like a quiet celebration.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它们排在窗台上，字牌一个接一个开始嗡鸣，在墙上投出五彩斑斓的影子，像一场无声的庆祝。

attention:2.en: Silverfang had been quiet for an hour, studying the spiral scratched into the lighthouse floor. Suddenly he called for our *attention*, pointing at the centre of the spiral where a tiny compass needle was set into the stone. It was spinning. Old Helm said a spinning needle meant a new island was rising somewhere close, still finding its place in the sky.
attention:2.cnHint: 银牙突然要大家把____集中到地板螺旋图案的中心。
attention:2.hook: The needle stopped spinning and pointed straight toward the open east.
attention:2.line: 'Your *attention*, please — this needle does not spin without a reason.'

sentences.en: Silverfang had been quiet for an hour, studying the spiral scratched into the lighthouse floor.
sentences.cn: 银牙安静了一个小时，研究着刻在灯塔地板上的螺旋纹。

sentences.en: Suddenly he called for our *attention*, pointing at the centre of the spiral where a tiny compass needle was set into the stone.
It was spinning.
sentences.cn: 它在旋转。

sentences.en: Old Helm said a spinning needle meant a new island was rising somewhere close, still finding its place in the sky.
sentences.cn: 老舵说指针旋转意味着有新的岛屿正在某处上升，还在寻找它在天空中的位置。

certain:2.en: Bell unrolled the message found inside the signal lantern and read it twice in silence. Then she told us she was *certain* the handwriting matched the notes in Old Helm's oldest logbook — the one he kept from his very first voyage. Old Helm went pale, then smiled a slow, wondering smile, as if the sky had just handed him back something long lost.
certain:2.cnHint: 小铃____地认出，信上的笔迹与老舵手最早的航行日志出自同一人。
certain:2.hook: Old Helm turned to the last page of the logbook and found it blank no more.
certain:2.line: 'I am *certain* — I have studied that handwriting for twenty years.'

sentences.en: Bell unrolled the message found inside the signal lantern and read it twice in silence.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开信号灯里找到的信息，默默读了两遍。

sentences.en: Then she told us she was *certain* the handwriting matched the notes in Old Helm's oldest logbook — the one he kept from his very first voyage.
Old Helm went pale, then smiled a slow, wondering smile, as if the sky had just handed him back something long lost.
sentences.cn: 老舵脸色变白，随后绽开一个缓缓的、惊奇的笑容，仿佛天空刚刚把什么失落已久的东西还给了他。
